title: Spiritual Gifts in the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Spiritual gifts in the church are graces given by the Holy Spirit for serving others, building up the body, and glorifying Christ. Gifts are not badges of superiority, but tools for love and edification.
summary: Spiritual gifts in the church are graces given by the Holy Spirit for serving others, building up the body, and glorifying Christ. Gifts are not badges of superiority, but tools for love and edification.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives gifts to His church by the Spirit so His people may be built up into maturity. Gifts must serve His body, honor His Word, and display His love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit gives gifts to believers according to God’s wisdom. The gifts differ, but they come from the same Spirit and are meant for the common good.

Spiritual gifts are not given for pride, comparison, disorder, or personal platform. They are given for service, edification, and the glory of God in Christ.

The body needs many kinds of gifts. Visible and hidden service both matter. Teaching, mercy, generosity, encouragement, leadership, helps, and other forms of grace serve the health of the church.

Love must govern the use of gifts. Without love, even impressive gifts become empty and harmful. Gifts are healthiest when they build others up and point away from self toward Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Confusion about gifts can create pride, jealousy, passivity, or spiritual competition. Some believers exalt certain gifts, while others assume they have nothing meaningful to offer.

This doctrine reminds the church that the Spirit gives gifts for the body. The question is not “How can my gift make me important?” but “How can I serve Christ’s people in love?”

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use whatever grace God has given you to serve others. Do not envy another believer’s gift or despise your own. Seek love, order, humility, and edification. Let your gifts strengthen the church and glorify Christ rather than drawing attention to yourself.
